Arnold Vosloo

By: Hein Kaiser | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
we catch up with South African acting legend Arnold Vosloo who's in the country

Unique Selling Point:
- Arnold Vosloo along with Charlize Theron were trailblazers for South African talent in the US film industry.
- Arnold celebrates three decades in showbusiness this year.
- Arnold was inducted into the Emperors Palace Walk of Fame alongside previous inductee Derek Watts
- Arnold speaks candidly about his career and what it's like in Hollywood.
- Local boytjie made it big.

Summary:
With more than 90 appearances on the big and small screen, South African actor Arnold Vosloo has become a South African, and Hollywood legend.

After leaving South Africa almost three decades ago, Arnold has made his mark in Hollywood with blockbuster movies like the Mummy and starring opposite Leonardo Di Caprio in Blood Diamonds.

He recently wrapped up his latest feature film, one of two shot in South Africa during the past five years, and this week Arnold’s handprints were immortalized at Emperor’s Palace Hall of Fame in Johannesburg.

But it all started for Arnold in the early eighties when he landed a role in South African cinema legend Jamie Uys’s candid camera movie Funny People 2. It then led him to a leading role in the box office hit Boetie Gaan Border Toe and the rest, as they say in the classics, is history…

Script:


00:00:06:09 - 00:00:36:00
It all started 36 years ago when he starred as Boetie in the 1984 film Boetie Gaan Border Toe. It broke box office records at the time and turned actor Arnold Vosloo into an overnight household name. But Boetie didn't stay on the border, he decided to head for Hollywood. One giant leap for a young South African. Arnold. Great to meet you. And thanks for giving us this time.

00:00:36:13 - 00:00:42:25
Thank you, Derek
We've we've never done this. Of course, you're a legend here and my first time, so be gentle.

00:00:43:26 - 00:00:45:00
Sometimes people.

00:00:45:03 - 00:00:45:18
Call it.

00:00:45:23 - 00:00:48:22
Derek: Being a relic,
Arnold: A legend,.


00:00:50:28 - 00:00:58:17
Derek: I'm going to take Legend - Arnold. It was your parents who really set the stage for you?

00:00:58:29 - 00:01:09:26
Arnold: Yes, absolutely. My parents were both in the business way back touring with the old National Theatre. And then my father started a movie company.

00:01:10:03 - 00:01:40:03
VO: It was, after booting this boy from Albertson, leapt into the big time. And even though Hollywood was always an ambition, love was the catalyst that finally led him to the bright lights on movement. His first wife, American actress Nancy Mulford, on set during the filming of his first international starring roles. Acts of Piracy and Skeleton Coast were filmed in Namibia. They got married and moved to the States.

00:01:40:17 - 00:01:59:25
Arnold: I'd always wanted to go, and the Nancy happened in my life and suddenly I found myself there and I thought, no, you know, I'm really going to give it a go. And I came back and told my parents and my sister at the time, this is it, guys. I'm going to go over there now and give it a shot and and got on the plane and went.

00:02:00:02 - 00:02:05:12
VO: Going from fame at home to no name in the States wasn't easy for young Arnold.

00:02:05:21 - 00:02:18:20
Arnold: Certainly the first two years were tough. I always tell the story of one of the first auditions that I went on. They were like 500 guys, you know, around the block in a line and four of them look like me.

00:02:19:03 - 00:02:20:18
So I'm like, What?

00:02:20:23 - 00:02:30:15
Arnold: What makes you think you're going to get this job? So people knew who I was here, and suddenly I was over there and people were like, Arnold, who, you know, get in line. That's me. Yeah.

00:02:31:15 - 00:02:41:26
Arnold: Yeah, that's how I looked in the play.

Derek: So you went through this long struggle to get known in America. Did you think of packing up and coming home?

00:02:43:12 - 00:03:07:02
You know, when I was working in American with bleak days, I just didn't have anything. You know, no job for three months. I would sometimes think about coming back, but then something and I don't know what it is. Once again, it's ego or or madness. What you just sort of say, no, the hell with it. You know, I'm going to I'm going to spit in their faces. I'm going to vanquish them. You know, I'm going to do this.

00:03:07:13 - 00:03:19:26
VO: Ironically, a play called Born in the RSA that told the United States gave Arnold his first big break. That's where he was spotted by a major agent and signed up backstage.

00:03:20:07 - 00:03:44:27
I remember calling my late father, Daan, and saying, Hey, I just took this job, you know, and I'm going I'm going to stay and do the job in New Orleans. And he was like, No, we missed you. You got to come back. And I was like, Well, Dad, you know, I think they're going to pay me, like, $60,000 or whatever the amount was 20 years ago. There was, like, a silence on the line. My father's, like, acting.
“jy moet bly” used to do that. You just don't do the movie.

VO: Arnold staked his claim in Hollywood. First big break came when he starred as the bad guy in the 1993 film Hard Target. His ability to play challenging parts caught the eye of the film's producers, who got in touch a few years later, offered him the role of a lifetime as the baddie Imhotep in The Mummy.

00:04:10:10 - 00:04:18:27
Arnold: The Mummy movies were so big. I mean, even to this day, it's amazing to me how popular and how big those two films were.

00:04:19:24 - 00:04:32:07
Derek: The Mummy became one of the most successful movie franchises at the time, taking more than $1,000,000,000 at the box office and spawning a host of sequels and spinoffs. Did they set you up?

00:04:32:09 - 00:05:01:15
Arnold: Financially, yes, absolutely. They set me up financially. Once films make the money back, you share in the profits. And those two mummy movies made over $1,000,000,000. And even to this day, some mother or father would come over to me and say, Are you the mummy? And I'd say, yes. Then they'd say, I'm so sick of your face. I see that movie four times a week and my kids watch it over and over and over and I'm sick of your face.

00:05:02:12 - 00:05:31:17
VO: Today, Arnold has more than 90 film appearances under his belt, several awards, and has played opposite some of the biggest names in entertainment, including Al Pacino, Kiefer Sutherland and Leonardo DiCaprio. Arnold may live in Santa Monica with his wife Silvia and dog Zuzu, but it's clear that his heart and soul are still in South Africa.

Derek: So when you come back, what makes you feel good about being back?

00:05:31:19 - 00:05:57:14
Arnold: Everything. There's the intangibles, you know, there's the sunsets that those things that just take your breath away and, you know, your favorite foods and drinking and Stoney ginger beer and Bar Ones and all those things. One of the cool things about COVID, and it's the only cool thing for a guy like me that's got a known face, is when you put a mask on and a hat, nobody recognizes you, right?

END
